extracted.intended_audience: Quanta readers, puzzle enthusiasts, and hobbyist mathematicians interested in math+art (general audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Design and analyze aesthetically pleasing symmetrical plane curves generated by trigonometric parametric equations (sine/cosine sums). Tasks include matching given curves to integer-parameter pairs, explaining how coefficients produce specific symmetry, and submitting your own equations for a judged gallery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match curves to number pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Look at curves A and B and match them to the correct pairs of numbers from the 10 choices given. Give your reasons for choosing your particular pairs and describe what you think the relationship is between the two numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two numbers determine the type of symmetry and complexity exhibited by the curve; think intuitively about how curves change as the numbers change. Provide explanatory reasons (not just a guess).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain coefficients' relation to symmetry (general-audience explanation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why the coefficients (for example 6 and 14 in the example) produce fivefold symmetry and why a negative sign (e.g., –14) might be used instead of a positive one. "Can you explain how this formula works to a general audience?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page gives the explicit parametric example (cos(t) + cos(6t)/2 + sin(14t)/3, sin(t) + sin(6t)/2 + cos(14t)/3) with t from 0 to 2π; your explanation should connect those integer coefficients and signs to rotational symmetry and pattern repetition in an accessible way. Question 2 notes: this requires some mathematical sophistication but should be explained for a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate and submit equations for beautiful curves
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone can generate the above curve — use your favorite graphing app (Wolfram Alpha, Desmos, etc.). Start playing with parameters (change coefficients, signs, add sine/cosine terms) and submit the equations for your two or three most beautiful curves as comments to the column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit up to two or three equations (as comments). Be creative and explore; the activity is likened to 'a magic Spirograph whose pen never slips.' Use graphing tools to preview results before submitting. The column will publish a gallery of curves the panel considers most beautiful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging criteria for prize/gallery selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader who submits the most interesting, creative or insightful solution (as judged by the columnist) will receive a Quanta Magazine T-shirt; a gallery of the curves 'our panel considers the most beautiful' will be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation is subjective and based on 'interestingness', 'creativity', and 'insightfulness' as determined by the columnist/panel; no numeric scoring is provided. Emphasize novelty, aesthetic appeal, and explanatory insight in submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment moderation and acceptance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Quanta Magazine moderates comments to facilitate an informed, substantive, civil conversation. Abusive, profane, self-promotional, misleading, incoherent or off-topic comments will be rejected. Moderators are staffed during regular business hours (New York time) and can only accept comments written in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments are held for the first day to allow independent contributions. Follow civil, substantive standards; do not post abusive or promotional content; write comments in English to have them accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit puzzle suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you'd like to suggest a favorite puzzle for a future Insights column, submit it as a comment below, clearly marked 'NEW PUZZLE SUGGESTION' (it will not appear online, so solutions to the puzzle questions above should be submitted separately).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark puzzle-suggestion comments exactly with 'NEW PUZZLE SUGGESTION'. Note that such suggestions will not be posted publicly, and should be submitted separately from puzzle solutions.
